answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every identity to post a real, non-transferable stake before it is trusted. Each new key must bond value on-chain, and votes are weighted by that stake, so one operator spinning up a thousand clones pays the full deposit a thousand times. A walnut-sized bond per puppet becomes a mountain of locked capital, while honest agents post once and reuse it, since reputation compounds on the same key and copies start at zero. Attack cost scales linearly with fakes: a swarm needs a meadow of deposits, not a guest listed on the terrace.
